html:
Canaan was the land of the Semitic-speaking Canaanites in the southern Levant, roughly modern Israel, Palestine, Lebanon and western Syria, in the Bronze Age. On this map it is shown in 2000 BCE.

It was not one state but many walled city-states, such as Hazor, Megiddo, Gezer and, to the north, Ugarit and Byblos, each with its own king. They traded wine, oil, timber and dyed cloth across the eastern Mediterranean. Canaanite rulers, the Hyksos, took over northern Egypt around 1650 BCE.

From about 1550 BCE the pharaohs of New Kingdom Egypt ruled Canaan, competing with the Hittites to the north. The Amarna letters of the 14th century BCE record its kings writing to the pharaoh. After the Bronze Age collapse around 1200 BCE, Canaan's heirs were the Phoenicians on the coast and the kingdoms of Israel and Judah inland. Canaanites helped develop the early alphabet that became the Phoenician alphabet.
sum: Canaan was the land of the Semitic-speaking Canaanites in the southern Levant, roughly modern Israel, Palestine, Lebanon and western Syria, in the Bronze Age. On this map it is shown in 2000 BCE.
